name: VFBquery API
description: Query services for Virtual Fly Brain — term information, search, connectivity, cross-references, FlyBase stocks and the hosted-CATMAID pass-through. All endpoints are read-only GETs returning JSON.

endpoints.summary: Full term report for one VFB/FBbt id
endpoints.description: The report behind the website's term information panel: metadata, synonyms, relationships, aligned images, cross-references, and the list of queries that can be run from the term.

params.name: force_refresh
params.doc: Force a cache clear: bypasses the edge cache and makes VFBquery recompute now. Refreshes the canonical URL directly, so this call and the very next one — even unticked — both return fresh data.

endpoints.summary: Run one of a term's named queries
endpoints.description: Executes one of the query types listed in a term's Queries section (see /get_term_info). Results are the website's own row format; offset/limit page them.

params.name: query_type
params.doc: One of the named query types

params.name: include_graph
params.doc: true adds a graph rendering of the rows

params.name: force_refresh
params.doc: Force a cache clear: bypasses the edge cache and makes VFBquery recompute now. Refreshes the canonical URL directly, so this call and the very next one — even unticked — both return fresh data.

endpoints.summary: Partonomy / subclass tree around a term
endpoints.description: The hierarchy browser's tree: follow one relationship from a term, upward, downward or both.
The canonical ranked search the site uses. filter/exclude/boost/demote take type names — GET /facets lists every accepted name.
The vocabulary for /search's four type parameters.
Both directions of the cross-reference mapping. Give id= for VFB → external, or accession= (optionally with db=) for external → VFB.

params.name: db
params.doc: Restrict to one site (name, symbol or nickname)

endpoints.description: Combine two or more named queries with OR/AND/NOT/XOR (and friends), compared on term id. Name each operand as its own parameter, then reference the names in expr. The response traces every step.

params.name: expr
params.doc: Boolean expression over the operand names

endpoints.summary: Connectome datasets in the knowledge graph
endpoints.description: The datasets /query_connectivity can draw on, with their labels and symbols.
Connections from one neuron type (or any subclass) to another, summed across the connectomes. Types are labels, synonyms or FBbt ids.

params.name: upstream_type
params.doc: Presynaptic type (label, synonym or FBbt id)

params.name: group_by_class
params.doc: true groups rows by neuron class

params.name: force_refresh
params.doc: Force a cache clear: bypasses the edge cache and makes VFBquery recompute now. Refreshes the canonical URL directly, so this call and the very next one — even unticked — both return fresh data.

endpoints.summary: Predicted neurotransmitter(s) for a neuron type
endpoints.description: Predicted neurotransmitters for a neuron type (or any subclass), from per-instance prediction edges. Aggregated to flat per-class rows by default; optionally split by dataset. Reported as GO secretion terms with mean confidence.

params.name: neuron_type
params.doc: Neuron type (label, synonym or FBbt id)

params.name: aggregate
params.doc: false returns per-instance rows (default true aggregates to the class)

params.name: split_by_dataset
params.doc: true adds a dataset column and one row per dataset

params.name: force_refresh
params.doc: Force a cache clear: bypasses the edge cache and makes VFBquery recompute now. Refreshes the canonical URL directly, so this call and the very next one — even unticked — both return fresh data.

endpoints.summary: Known (curated) neurotransmitter(s) for a neuron type
endpoints.description: Curated neurotransmitters for a neuron type and its subclasses, from ontology classification (no confidence). One row per (cell type, GO secretion term); empty when the ontology asserts none.

params.name: neuron_type
params.doc: Neuron type (label, synonym or FBbt id)

params.name: force_refresh
params.doc: Force a cache clear: bypasses the edge cache and makes VFBquery recompute now. Refreshes the canonical URL directly, so this call and the very next one — even unticked — both return fresh data.

endpoints.description: Free-text resolver for FlyBase features; returns candidate ids for /find_stocks.
Stock-centre holdings for a resolved feature id.
Publications using a resolved FBco combination.
Every hosted instance with its metadata, projects, anonymous read-only token, and the knowledge-graph cross-reference site used for VFB id ↔ skeleton id conversion.
Instance details plus the full command registry with per-command documentation.

The curated CATMAID query surface. Commands taking skeleton ids accept CATMAID skids, VFB ids, or a mixed comma-separated list — VFB ids are converted through the knowledge graph before the request is made, and the response envelope maps ids both ways. raw=true returns the untouched CATMAID payload. Unrecognised parameters are forwarded to CATMAID verbatim. For swc, aligned= names a template space for VFB's registered copy, and the swc_alignments command lists the spaces available. Every command also has its own runnable card in the expanded section below. Also accepts POST: put the same parameters in a JSON object body (or an application/x-www-form-urlencoded/multipart form) instead of the query string — the only way to send an id list too long for a URL. project and raw stay on the query string either way; a GET and the equivalent POST share one cache entry. The Run button below only exercises GET — for example, curl -X POST '/catmaid/fafb/annotations_for_skeletons' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"ids": [1, 2, 3]}'.

params.name: ids
params.doc: Skeleton ids and/or VFB ids, comma-separated (list commands)

params.name: id
params.doc: One skeleton id or VFB id (single-id commands)

params.name: project
params.doc: CATMAID project id (defaults to the instance's first project)

params.name: raw
params.doc: true returns the untouched CATMAID response

endpoints.summary: Queue depth, cache stats, worker utilisation

annotations_for_skeletons.doc: Annotations on each of a set of skeletons.

annotations_query_targets.doc: Find neurons/annotations by annotation or name (name=, annotated_with=, types[0]=neuron, ...).

circles_of_hell.doc: Skeletons within n hops of the given set (n_circles=1, ...).

compact_detail.doc: Compact treenode representation for a set of skeletons (with_connectors=, with_tags=, ...).

connectivity_counts.doc: Synapse counts by link type per skeleton.

connectivity_matrix.doc: Sparse connectivity matrix between two skeleton sets.

connector_info.doc: Detailed information on one connector (path id is a raw connector id).

connector_links.doc: Connector links on a set of skeletons (relation_type=presynaptic_to|postsynaptic_to|...).

eswc.doc: Skeleton as extended SWC text (creator/edit metadata).

find_label_nodes.doc: Find nodes whose labels match a query (query=).

list_skeletons.doc: List skeleton ids by filter (nodecount_gt=, created_by=, ...).

nearest_node.doc: Closest node to a location (x=, y=, z=).

neuroglancer_skeleton.doc: Skeleton in neuroglancer precomputed format (base64 in the JSON envelope).

neuron_ids.doc: CATMAID neuron id for each skeleton id.

neuron_names.doc: Map skeleton ids to neuron names.

neuron_skeletons.doc: All skeleton ids modelling a neuron. id= accepts a skid or VFB id; the CATMAID neuron id is derived automatically.

node_locations.doc: Locations for a set of node ids (node_ids[0]=..., raw node ids, not skeleton ids).

projects.doc: List projects visible on this instance.

sampler_count.doc: Number of reconstruction samplers per skeleton.

skeleton_cable_length.doc: Cable length of a single skeleton.

skeleton_compact_detail.doc: Compact treenode representation of one skeleton (with_connectors=, with_tags=, ...).

skeleton_node_overview.doc: Treenode / review / label overview of one skeleton.

skeleton_root.doc: Root treenode id and location of a skeleton.

skeleton_summary.doc: Summary information (node counts, cable, review) per skeleton.

skeleton_validity.doc: Which of the given skeleton ids exist in the project.

skeletons_in_bounding_box.doc: Skeleton ids intersecting a bounding box (minx=..maxz=, min_nodes=, ...).

skeletons_within_distance.doc: Skeletons with nodes within a distance of a location.

swc.doc: Skeleton as SWC text. aligned=<template short_form or label> returns VFB's copy registered to that template instead of the original EM-space skeleton (aligned=vfb picks the VFB copy while there is only one; aligned=original or omitted is the CATMAID original).

swc_alignments.doc: List the spaces an swc download is available in for one neuron: the original EM space plus any VFB template-registered copies. Each row carries the aligned= value to pass to swc.

treenode_info.doc: Skeleton/neuron information for one treenode (path id is a raw treenode id).
